scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

estimate substitution when no accepted read

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-REQUESTER-FRAMING.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

H-AMI-READ-FAILURE.statement: AMI read failures or missing reads since August have led to increased estimation and incorrect bills, driving dispute volume.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change in billing import validation rules after August introduced systematic billing errors, increasing disputes.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: Declines in successful manual meter reads (field route completion) since August have increased reliance on estimation, causing billing errors and disputes.

H-HANDOFF-DELAY.statement: Latency or corruption in the nightly MDMS-to-billing handoff since August has resulted in missing or delayed reads, leading to estimation errors and disputes.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route completion for Aug‑Sep is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating a decline in successful manual meter reads that could increase estimation and billing disputes.
Dispute ticket volume rose sharply in August and remained high in September, roughly doubling compared to June‑July levels.

The tariff change log in the billing database contains no records, indicating that no tariff changes were logged during the observed period, thus tariff changes are not a likely cause of the dispute surge.

The observation shows that among disputed bills, more are associated with actual reads (1,785) than estimated reads (1,240). This indicates that billing disputes are not driven solely by estimation errors; issues also arise from bills based on actual meter reads.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The field operations manager reports a shortage of three meter readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in estimated bills for affected customers. This staffing gap likely increases reliance on estimation and could contribute to billing disputes.

The observation shows median dispute response time of 1.6 days and 90th percentile of 2.8 days, both within the 3‑day SLA, with 2,440 tickets processed. This indicates that the dispute surge is not due to slow response times; response performance meets the agreed service level.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports no tariff changes this year, indicating tariff changes are not driving the dispute surge.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract confirms that route priority changes can be requested by the utility but must be executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation, reinforcing the existing authorization requirement for dispatch changes; it does not speak to billing rule changes or the cause of the dispute surge.

structural_remedies.description: Audit the billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES) for any entries after August; if a post‑August change is found, revert the rule set to the pre‑August baseline and document the change.
structural_remedies.rationale: Log review is a read‑only operation on DA-RULES; no bill writes are required, satisfying K‑BILLWRITE, and can be completed well within the remaining 225 minutes.; residual gap: If the audit finds no rule change after August, the root cause remains unknown and the dispute surge may stem from another source (e.g., actual‑read validation or handoff latency). In that case further analysis is needed to identify the true cause.

hypotheses.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.
hypotheses.rationale: If the requester's framing is correct, the solution is an AI agent to auto-answer tickets; otherwise a different root-cause fix is needed.

hypotheses.statement: AMI read failures or missing reads since August have led to increased estimation and incorrect bills, driving dispute volume.
hypotheses.rationale: If AMI/MDMS data are deficient, fixing the data pipeline (meter reads, validation) is required; an AI agent would not resolve the underlying billing errors.

hypotheses.statement: A change in billing import validation rules after August introduced systematic billing errors, increasing disputes.
hypotheses.rationale: If validation rules are at fault, correcting the rule set and rebilling affected accounts is needed; an AI agent would not stop the generation of wrong bills.

hypotheses.statement: Declines in successful manual meter reads (field route completion) since August have increased reliance on estimation, causing billing errors and disputes.
hypotheses.rationale: If field read gaps are the cause, improving field operations or read acquisition would reduce disputes; an AI agent would only treat symptoms.

hypotheses.statement: Latency or corruption in the nightly MDMS-to-billing handoff since August has resulted in missing or delayed reads, leading to estimation errors and disputes.
hypotheses.rationale: If the handoff is unreliable, fixing the data transfer process (schedule, validation) is required; an AI agent would not prevent the root cause of wrong bills.

actions.question: dispute_volume_monthly

actions.why_now: High decision impact and low cost; essential first step.

actions.question: disputed_bills_by_read_type
actions.expected_information_gain: Splits disputed bills by read type (manual vs AMI) to see whether errors cluster with field reads or AMI reads.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: If disputes are concentrated in manual‑read bills, field‑gap hypothesis gains support; if in AMI‑read bills, AMI‑failure or handoff hypotheses gain support.
actions.why_now: Directly discriminates between the leading technical hypotheses at modest cost.

actions.question: route_completion_aug_sep
actions.expected_information_gain: Measures successful manual meter‑read completion for Aug‑Sep to test whether field‑read gaps have worsened.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: A significant drop in completion rates would substantiate the field‑read‑gap hypothesis and explain increased estimation.
actions.why_now: Low‑cost, high‑discriminative‑power test for the field‑gap hypothesis.

actions.question: read_events_for_disputed_estimated
actions.expected_information_gain: Provides AMI read events for the subset of bills that ended up estimated, revealing whether missing AMI reads drove estimation.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: If many disputed‑estimated bills lack AMI reads, the AMI‑failure or handoff‑delay hypotheses are strengthened.
actions.why_now: Addresses the AMI‑read‑failure and handoff‑delay hypotheses; cost reflects potential vendor provisioning.

actions.question: tariff_change_log
actions.expected_information_gain: Shows any tariff or billing‑import validation rule changes after August that could have introduced systematic billing errors.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: A rule change correlated with the dispute surge would strongly support the billing‑rule‑change hypothesis.
actions.why_now: Inexpensive, high‑confidence test for the billing‑rule hypothesis.
